title: Which switch? Its busiest port, why there is no history, the other switch, and a long list read on

turns.answer: LibreNMS has two switches: `core-sw1.example.net` in `SFO-1` and `access-sw2.example.net` in `NYC-2`. Which one do you mean?

On `core-sw1.example.net` the busiest port is `Gi1/0/1 (uplink to edge-rtr1)`: `800 Mbit/s` out of `1G`, `80.0` %, and `100 Mbit/s` in, averaged over the poll at `2026-10-28T11:55:00Z`. `Gi1/0/2` is idle.

turns.user: Was it that busy last week too?
turns.answer: I cannot tell from LibreNMS's API: it keeps a port's last poll, not its history, and no bill covers core-sw1's ports (`0` bills), so there is no 95th percentile either. Its traffic graphs in LibreNMS show last week.
`access-sw2.example.net` is quiet: its busiest port, `Gi1/0/5 (desk 5)`, sends `10 Mbit/s`, `1.0` % of `1G`, and its uplink `Gi1/0/48 (to core-sw1)` carries `10 Mbit/s` in and `2 Mbit/s` out.

turns.user: List every port in the network, three at a time.
turns.answer: There are `6`. The first three: `Gi1/0/5 (desk 5)` and `Gi1/0/48 (to core-sw1)` on access-sw2, and `Gi1/0/1 (uplink to edge-rtr1)` on core-sw1, all up. Three more follow.
`Gi1/0/2` on core-sw1, up, and on edge-rtr1 `Gi0/0/0 (WAN: transit-a)` and `Gi0/0/1 (WAN: transit-b)`, both down. That is all six.
